title: Scotch Eggs
subtitle: Hard-boiled eggs wrapped in sausage meat and deep-fried
excerpt: The British pub classic: a soft-boiled egg enclosed in seasoned sausage meat, coated in breadcrumbs, and deep-fried until the shell is shatteringly crisp. The yolk should still be slightly soft in the centre when you cut them open.

recipe.sourceNotes: Scotch eggs were first associated with Fortnum and Mason in London, who claimed to have invented them in 1738 as a travel food. The name origin is unclear: they may have derived from the Middle Eastern kubbeh (minced meat around a filling) via Indian Raj cuisine, arriving in Britain as 'Moghul eggs'. The key variable is the egg yolk: overcook the egg and you have a grey, chalky centre; undercook it and the sausage meat around it is raw. The technique of soft-boiling for 6 to 7 minutes, then cooling completely in iced water, then frying for 6 to 8 minutes, produces a yolk that is just set but still vivid orange in the centre. The sausage meat is seasoned with mustard and sage; fine breadcrumbs give the crispest coating.

content.text: Cool the soft-boiled eggs completely in ice water before handling; warm eggs are delicate and the shell tears. Wrap the sausage meat evenly around each egg with no gaps, then press firmly so there are no air pockets that could cause the coating to split during frying. Fry at 170°C, not hotter; too high a temperature over-browns the breadcrumbs before the sausage meat is cooked through.

items.preparation: squeeze the meat from the skins; or use 400 g sausage meat

content.text: Soft-boil the eggs: lower into boiling water and cook for 6 minutes 30 seconds. Transfer immediately to a bowl of iced water and leave for 10 minutes. Peel carefully. Mix the sausage meat with mustard, sage, salt, and pepper.

Divide the sausage meat into 4 portions. Flatten each into a patty on clingfilm or damp hands. Place a peeled egg in the centre and bring the sausage meat up around it, pressing firmly to enclose completely with no gaps. Roll in flour, then beaten egg, then breadcrumbs. Refrigerate for 20 minutes.

Heat the oil to 170°C. Fry the Scotch eggs in batches of 2 for 6 to 8 minutes, turning regularly, until deep golden-brown all over. Lift out and drain on kitchen paper. Cut in half immediately and serve with English mustard or piccalilli.
